discussion_comments.comment_body: On LM Studio's `/api/v0/models`, `max_context_length` is the model's ceiling, and a loaded model also reports `loaded_context_length`, which is what it actually serves (can be a lot smaller). Since maxInputTokens falls back to contextWindow and that's the compaction budget, compaction won't kick in before LM Studio starts rejecting. Prefer `loaded_context_length` when it's present?

Real, thanks. Both call sites already built a context for the adjacent `composeAiSdkProviderOptions` call, so it is now hoisted into a variable and passed to `resolvePortableReasoning` as well. Worth noting they would have thrown rather than mis-typed if a bedrock request ever reached them; they only passed because the short-circuit on providerId ran first.
is this pattern present elsewhere in the codebase? seems like special handling for bedrock which I'd like to avoid if possible
what do you think about making a pr upstream to the ai-sdk itself to fix the bedrock adapter so that it doesn't accidentally send reasoning. seems like the better place for the fix to live

discussion_comments.comment_body: Correct, and thanks for the precision. Registering the model only takes model *selection* off the catalog; `resolveBedrockModelId` still consults it, and with #14480 on main the bare `openai.gpt-6-astra` case goes out as `us.openai.gpt-6-astra` in us-east-1. The test now captures the request path: the `us.*` and `global.*` cases assert they pass through unchanged (no catalog involved), and the bare case is named for what it checks, that the OpenAI shape comes out whichever profile the resolver picks. Comment and PR description narrowed accordingly.
